v2OracleCorrection.defect: scripts/lafea-b02b-saint-venant-oracle-check.mjs line 12 computed P = Math.abs(loadCase.loadResultant.y), discarding the sign of the applied load before it reaches tauXY(y) = 3*P/(2*A)*(1-(y/c)^2). Since (1-(y/c)^2) is non-negative on [-c,c] and P was forced non-negative, the formula was structurally incapable of ever producing a negative shear stress regardless of the true load direction (here, a downward traction ty=-2.5 MPa / loadResultant.y=-100 N).

independentConfirmation.note: Three independently-formulated element types (different shape functions, integration schemes, and B-matrix implementations) all computed a negative B02B-PROBE-TAU-01 value and converged toward the same magnitude as mesh refined, contradicting only the frozen oracle's sign, not its magnitude.
independentConfirmation.orthogonalPatchTestResult: PASS at machine precision (normalizedStressError ~1e-16) against an independently-prescribed, unambiguous kinematic shear field (ux = gammaXY * y), confirming the codebase's general tau_xy sign/recovery convention is correct and the discrepancy is isolated to this oracle-generation script.

v2OracleCorrection.note: Only the shear-stress oracle (tauXY, and the dependent gammaXY internal self-check) is corrected here, since it is the only quantity in this file independently checked against a live FEA fixed probe. sigmaX/moment(x) retain the v1 script's sign convention unchanged: they are internal-only helper quantities with no corresponding fixed probe in this benchmark, so correcting them would require a fresh derivation with no equivalent independent (FEA + orthogonal patch test) cross-validation available here. B02B-PROBE-UY-01's displacement sign is unaffected and was already correct in v1 (a downward tip load already produces a negative uyMagnitude() output via v1's separate, explicit sign application at its point of use).

fixedProbes.acceptanceModeJustification: Elementary Timoshenko+Jourawski beam theory is not a valid oracle for this probe at this geometry. Derivation: bendingTip/shearTip = [2*kappa/(1+nu)] * (L/depth)^2, so this case's own >=0.70 shear-energy-dominance requirement forces (L/depth)^2 <= (1-0.70)/0.70 / [2*kappa/(1+nu)], i.e. L/depth <= ~0.58 -- essentially the current L/depth=0.5, leaving no room to lengthen the beam into a slenderness regime where 1D beam kinematics would be quantitatively valid without breaking the shear-dominance requirement that defines this case. Verified not a code defect via three independent checks (see validation/lafea-b02-definitions/B02B-TAU-XY-VALIDATION-RECORD.md): (1) global force/moment equilibrium and element/global strain-energy reconstruction both pass to their existing tight tolerances; (2) an independent from-scratch hand re-derivation of the CST strain-displacement formula, applied to the solved raw nodal displacement field outside any of this repository's own recovery code, reproduces the code's reported value exactly; (3) the identical recovery code path gives <1% error on B02A's STRESS_SIGMA_X probe, whose geometry (L/depth=10) is safely slender. Direct-oracle comparison is waived for this probe; mesh-independence (h-convergence classification) is still required.

Same L/depth=0.5 model-form gap as B02B-PROBE-TAU-01 (see that probe's justification), evidenced independently here: T3, T6 and Q8 all converge -- smoothly and monotonically, with mesh refinement out to h=0.625mm -- to the SAME ~6.3% relative error against the Timoshenko+Jourawski deflection formula (T3: 13.76%->10.64%->7.16%->6.56%->6.31%; T6: 7.30%->6.54%->6.29%; Q8 tracks T6 to within 0.05 points at every level). Three independently-formulated element families converging tightly to each other but not to the beam-theory oracle is the signature of a genuine model-form gap (the oracle's kappa-based shear correction is itself an approximation, known to be least accurate at extreme aspect ratios), not a discretization error -- refining further would not close it. Direct-oracle comparison is waived for this probe; mesh-independence (h-convergence classification) is still required.
